summary: This is a humorous April 1st memo that creates a new RFC subseries called IETF Statements of Boredom. It is a joke.

plainLanguage.summary: This April 1st RFC jokes about creating a subseries for documents that say nothing useful. The proposed review process ends by discarding each document and leaving a vacuum.

questions: what are ietf statements of boredom
how does the fictional sob process work
does rfc 1438 define a real standard
subtitle: A satirical proposal for an RFC subseries that approves and then discards documents.

tldr.problem: The memo imagines a gap in the RFC process: no category for documents that express concern while containing no useful information.
tldr.mechanism: It proposes IETF Statements Of Boredom, reviewed through an elaborate process and discarded after reviewers fall asleep.
tldr.outcome: The proposal ends in a vacuum that, the memo says, cannot be an official Internet Standard.

today: RFC 1438 is an Informational satire of the RFC process. Its fictional SOB series is described as ending in discarded documents, not as an Internet standard.

sections.title: A New Category for Nothing
sections.content: The memo describes standards-track and other RFCs, then proposes an additional category for documents that express deep concern about something but contain no useful information. It names the proposed subseries IETF Statements Of Boredom, or SOBs.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal invents a category for documents whose only purpose is to express concern without useful content. The name is IETF Statements Of Boredom.

sections.title: The SOB Review Process
sections.content:
The fictional process sends an SOB to the IAB, IRSG, IESG, an SOB Editor named Morpheus, and the Academie Francais for review and other formal steps. Once everyone has approved the document by falling asleep over it, the process ends and the document is discarded.

The RFC says the resulting vacuum is viewed as having technical approval but is not, and cannot become, an official Internet Standard.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposed reviewers perform formal steps, then approve the document by falling asleep. The document is discarded, so the result is a vacuum rather than a standard.

sections.title: Status of the Memo
sections.content: RFC 1438 provides information and does not specify an Internet standard. Its description of a new subseries is presented as satire of the RFC process.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo uses a fictional process to make fun of standards procedures. It does not establish an Internet standard.

references.text: Internet Activities Board, "The Internet Standards Process", RFC 1310, March 1992.
Postel, J., Editor, "IAB Official Protocol Standards", RFC 1410, March 1993.
